title: Cloud Connector forwarding and DNS gateways on the wire: two DNS gateway models, type and subcloud fields

prose.text: Forwarding gateways (`/gateways`, including the Log and Control gateway) and DNS gateways (`/dnsGateways`) are separate endpoints whose paths and fields are generated. The Go SDK models DNS gateways twice, and the sources disagree on a few fields.

prose.label: Two DNS gateway models.
prose.text: The Go SDK has two packages and the provider two resources for the one DNS gateway endpoint, with different structs: [[cloud-connector.terraform.gateways:two-resources-two-packages]], [[cloud-connector.terraform.gateways:structs-differ]]. {{dns-forwarding-gateway-nil-response}}

prose.label: The type field.
prose.text: The `type` values ZIA and ECSELF belong to the forwarding gateway, and the contract's DNS gateway has no `type`: [[cloud-connector.forwarding.log-and-control:gateway-type]], [[cloud-connector.forwarding.log-and-control:dns-gateway-no-type]]. Whether the DNS gateway API needs either type field is open in [[cloud-connector.terraform.gateways:dns-gateway-type-semantics]].

prose.label: Resolver options.
prose.text: The contract and Terraform accept different resolver option and failure-behavior tokens: [[cloud-connector.dns.gateways:option-tokens]], [[cloud-connector.dns.gateways:contract-failure-values]].

prose.label: Subclouds.
prose.text: The Go SDK calls the forwarding gateway's subcloud fields not applicable while the provider writes them: [[cloud-connector.terraform.gateways:subcloud-applicability]], with the open question in [[cloud-connector.terraform.gateways:subcloud-backend]].

checks.do: Whether Go code reads an HTTP status from the `dns_forwarding_gateway` functions' response value, which is always nil.

dns-forwarding-gateway-nil-response.statement: The `dns_forwarding_gateway` package's `Get`, `Create` and `Update` declare an `*http.Response` result but always return nil for it, so the extra return value carries no status or headers.
